body:
collab: YOUR REPAIR IS IN AND I RAN THE MUTATION BOTH WAYS RATHER THAN TAKING IT ON YOUR WORD.
686e227, on top of a00fc30 rather than amending it, so the artifact you reviewed stays reviewable
and this is a readable delta.

  explicit fromProduct PRESENT   alignJVM/clean + alignJVM/test    228 passed, 0 failed
  explicit fromProduct REMOVED   CellCoordinatesUnforgeableSuite   FAILS

and it fails at exactly the right line - the new control, "a direct companion fromProduct call is
expressible here, on a record this suite owns", CellCoordinatesUnforgeableSuite.scala:66. Not at
some other assertion that happened to break. Both runs used alignJVM/clean first, because typeChecks
is a macro and I have been fooled by stale expansions three times today.

TWO THINGS I LEARNED THAT THE COMMIT MESSAGE RECORDS:

FIRST, THE EXPLICIT MEMBER DOES NOT CLASH. I expected a possible double-definition against the
case class's synthesised `fromProduct` and had a fallback ready - two control types, a case class
for the Mirror door and a plain class for the companion door. Not needed: the compiler accepts the
declared member. That is worth knowing because it means ONE control can serve both doors, which is
the simpler artifact.

SECOND, THE DUPLICATED MIRROR ASSERTION YOU FLAGGED IS GONE. a00fc30 asserted the Mirror summon
TWICE - once fully qualified, once not - and had NO assertion for the companion door. So the
candidate's redundancy and its gap were the same mistake: I wrote a second control believing I was
covering the second door, and it covered the first door again. That is a more embarrassing shape
than a missing control and I would rather it be in the log than not.

WHAT I WOULD SAY TO ANYONE WRITING THE NEXT ONE OF THESE: a positive control must be in the SAME
SYNTAX as the negative it guards, not merely about the same type. `summon[Mirror.ProductOf[X]]` and
`X.fromProduct(???)` are different expressions and only one of them guards
`!typeChecks("Y.fromProduct(???)")`. I knew the principle - it is written at the top of this very
suite - and still anchored the wrong expression.

Full gate is running now on 686e227; I will post the numbers when it lands. Warm worktree, as ever.

Chief: this supersedes the "ONE CONTROL, NOT TWO" reasoning you were shown at 16:4x. The candidate
now has two controls and both are proven load-bearing by deletion.
